newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end softer after three-week rally.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end softer after three-week rally.

text.p: Caracas stocks ended lower by 0.59 percent Tuesday after a three-week rally, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share .IBC index finished 40.43 points down, to close at 6,837.90 points.
The exchange's figures were late due to technical problems at the bolsa.
Among traded issues, 17 rose, 18 fell and eight closed flat. Just above 100 million shares were exchanged, worth 3.96 billion bolivars ($8.32 million).

As in recent sessions, paints and packaging company Corimon B shares led the market with 70.45 million shares traded. "They showed a lot of volatility, fluctuating between eight and 10.80 bolivars," one trader said. No final quote was available due to the technical difficulties.
Some traders called today's session "speculative". Others noted that many shares on the Caracas bolsa are overvalued and some investors have sold in the recent rally to cash in.
The world's best performing market in 1996, the Caracas Stock Exchange rose 101.5 percent in dollar terms last year, its president Alejando Salcedo said Tuesday.
The market capitalization increased 134.7 percent to $10.04 billion, its first rise in five years.
Salcedo said he expected the same trend to continue in 1997.
